title: Opening a drawer must move keyboard focus into it: to its autofocus field when it has one, otherwise to its first control
status: Open, labelled confirmed and needs-decision. A fix is proposed in pull request #43139, not merged at pinnedCommit. That pull request is never sent to the model.
summary: A closed drawer is visibility: hidden and becomes visible through the slide-in transition. showModal() runs its focusing steps while everything inside is still hidden, so focus falls back to body and the trigger behind the modal is inert.
expectedBehaviour: Opening a drawer moves focus into it: to the [autofocus] element when there is one, otherwise to its first focusable control, as the HTML dialog focusing steps specify.
dependencies: dist/css/bootstrap.min.css: the published 6.0.0-alpha.1 stylesheet from npm (MIT); the repository does not commit built CSS
consumer: Author-written shoe listing with a filters drawer opened through data-bs-toggle, around the unchanged TypeScript source at pinnedCommit, served with types erased by Node's built-in stripping. The drawer has an autofocus search field (no name, so it is not part of the form data) for the stricter task. A second drawer (Sort) without an autofocus element is on the page.
addedAfterReview: Added after reviewing the engine-v13 patch for bootstrap6-drawer-initial-focus-autofocus: it focused an [autofocus] element and did nothing otherwise, so a drawer without one still dropped focus to the page body. That stricter case had replaced the base expectation instead of adding to it. The page now has both kinds of drawer, and one keyboard task needs both to take focus. Earlier patches are replayed against it without inference.
